hostRules.description: Authenticated ghcr.io lookups. Mend's hosted env fails to resolve ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner ('no-result' every run) even though anonymous registry access and local Renovate both work — so the github-runner app silently got no update PRs. A read:packages PAT uploaded as GHCR_TOKEN in the Mend Developer Portal (developer.mend.io -> repo settings -> Credentials) fixes both plausible causes (the actions org rejecting Mend's app token, or shared-egress rate limits).

packageRules.description: Docker digest-only refreshes (same tag, new sha) have no release timestamp on lscr.io/ghcr, so the renovate/stability-days check pends FOREVER and automerge can never fire — those PRs sat open indefinitely. Same-tag rebuilds skip the age gate; the 14-day supply-chain quarantine stays intact for real version bumps. ignoreTests is required on top of the null age gate: dropping stability-days left digest PRs with ZERO status checks, and in a repo with no CI Renovate won't automerge a check-less PR without it (internalChecksAsSuccess has no internal checks to count here).

Automerge GitHub Actions bumps too (they were excluded from the docker-compose automerge rule and sat open forever). Version bumps stay behind the top-level 14-day gate, which works for them because tag/release datasources carry timestamps.

GitHub Actions digest updates (tag re-pointing) turn out to have the same no-timestamp problem as Docker digests, despite the earlier assumption that GitHub provides one: PR #40 (actions/checkout digest to v7.0.1) sat with renovate/stability-days pending for 18 days — the status refreshed daily and stayed pending well past the commit (2026-07-17) and release (2026-07-20) dates — so it needed a manual merge on 2026-08-07. Same exemption as the Docker digest rule: skip the age gate and ignoreTests so the check-less PR can automerge. Real github-actions version bumps keep the full 14-day gate.

Stateful infra in the buzz app must never automerge majors: a Postgres major refuses to start on the previous major's data dir (pg_upgrade is a manual migration — exactly what took the relay down on 2026-07-31 when postgres 17->18 automerged and shipped as an app update). Majors here open a PR and wait for a human — the pg-migrate one-shot automates the data migration, but the compose (pg-migrate's pinned old major, PGDATA path, retire paths) must be updated in the same PR.

The buzz pg-migrate one-shot intentionally stays on the PREVIOUS Postgres major — its whole job is dumping the old-major cluster during the major upgrade — so never propose version bumps for it (digest refreshes are fine). Its pin moves by hand in the same PR as the next major.

customManagers.description: Bump the version: field in each umbrel-app.yml in lockstep with its app's Docker image
